Added a full language selector with 18 built-in translations, replacing the single \"Force English UI\" toggle.
Automatic migration: users who had \"Force English UI\" enabled keep their English UI through the new selector, no action required.
Critical fix for Android 8–12 crashes caused by JGit 7.x depending on InputStream.readAllBytes() (API 33+); now on JGit 5.13.3.
.gitignore fixes: patterns like **/generated/** now match files at the project root, and [abc] / [!abc] character classes are honored.
svg is no longer classified as binary, and lockfiles can be force-included via Inclusions.
Five recursive tree walks converted to iterative ones, preventing StackOverflowError on pathological directory trees.
Git reference validation moved off the UI thread; the Generate button no longer freezes on large repositories.
The context-menu label now refreshes when the UI language changes, matching the rest of the plugin.
Unified the share helper so the SHARE action and the result-panel chip behave identically.
Removed dead code, fixed the Download/Downloads path mismatch in strings, and various minor reliability improvements.
Follow these steps to enable One Code For AI in your IDE.
Get the latest .apk from the official repository or the distribution channel.
Open the APK on your device and accept the install from unknown sources if prompted.
Once installed, launch the CodeAssist app on your device.
Go to Settings > Plugins > Installed and enable One Code For AI. It will load automatically.
Close and reopen CodeAssist so all components load correctly.
Tap the project file tree in CodeAssist
The options context menu will open
The option to generate the dump will appear
Save the .txt to Download or send it to your AI

Find answers to common issues and learn how to get the most out of the plugin.
How do I disable Git functionality entirely?
Go to CodeAssist Settings, then Plugins, and open the One Code For AI settings. There you will find the \"Git integration\" toggle. When disabled, the plugin treats your folder as plain files.
Why does .gitignore still work when Git is disabled?
If Git is disabled, the plugin automatically searches your selected folder and its parent directories (up to 5 levels) for a .gitignore file. This ensures your filtering rules remain intact.
What do the amber .gitignore rules mean?
A rule is highlighted in amber when one of your manual inclusion or exclusion filters is actively overriding it. Inclusions and exclusions always take priority over .gitignore.
How do I use glob patterns in filters?
Use standard glob syntax: *.log (any log file), build/ (specific folder), **/generated/** (any nested generated folder). Tap the \"?\" icon next to the filter sections for a quick guide.
What do the new Android presets do?
Android (Kotlin) exports everything. Android (source only) strips tests and docs. Android (Resources) exports only XMLs (layouts/themes). They automatically exclude generated files like R.java.
Where are the settings for animations and notifications?
They are in the native CodeAssist settings for this plugin. Disabling animations helps performance on low-end devices. Disabling notifications silences progress and completion alerts.
How do I exclude an entire folder easily?
Open the file tree preview in the configuration dialog. Uncheck the folder you want to exclude. This is faster and safer than writing complex exclusion rules.
Can I cancel an export while it is running?
Yes. You can tap \"Cancel\" in the dialog, or simply dismiss the dialog. The export runs safely in the background and you can return to check its progress at any time.
Is my code uploaded to a server?
Absolutely not. The plugin does not require internet permission. All scanning, filtering, and generation happens 100% locally on your device.
Where are the generated files saved?
Exported files are saved to your device\'s public storage under Download/OneCodeForAI.

Whitelist of extensions and glob patterns, evaluated before .gitignore.

Supported syntax (same as .gitignore patterns):
- Extensions: kt, json, xml
- Wildcards: *.log, **/*.kt, src/*.kt
- Directories: build/, **/generated/**

Any file matching an inclusion is exported even if .gitignore or exclusions would skip it.

Inclusions take priority over exclusions and over .gitignore. Use it to force-include specific files or extensions.

Blacklist of extensions and glob patterns.

Supported syntax (same as .gitignore patterns):
- Extensions: log, tmp, pyc
- Wildcards: *.log, **/*.test.kt, src/*.bak
- Directories: build/, **/generated/**

Any file matching an exclusion is skipped, even if .gitignore would include it. Inclusions take priority over exclusions.

To exclude a specific folder without writing a pattern, use the file tree below.

Rules detected in the project's .gitignore file.

This list is read-only - edit .gitignore directly to change it.

Inclusions and exclusions take priority over these rules: adding a matching inclusion or exclusion forces the file in or out regardless of .gitignore. Overridden rules are highlighted in amber. Negated rules (starting with '!') are shown with a distinct background so they can be told apart from positive rules.

Binary files are detected by a fixed list of known binary extensions (images, video, audio, archives, compiled binaries, fonts, databases). Files with these extensions are skipped so the dump stays focused on readable source code.

Detection is extension-based only. To skip an uncommon binary format, add its extension to Exclusions. To force-include one, add it to Inclusions.

Disabling this toggle includes the listed extensions in the export, which is rarely useful for AI context.

Shows the project tree with every entry that matches the current filters. Uncheck any file or folder to exclude it from the export without writing an exclusion rule.

Excluding a folder automatically excludes its children. Re-including a single child inside an excluded folder restores only that entry, mirroring the behavior of .gitignore negation.

Use the header checkbox to include or exclude the entire project in one tap. The tree is a preview: it does not regenerate files, it only reflects the current inclusion state.

When enabled, files larger than the selected size are skipped. This protects the dump from a single huge file (e.g. a bundled asset or generated SQL) dominating the output.\n\nWhen disabled, every text file is included regardless of size, which can produce very large dumps. Combine it with the total export size limit in Settings to keep exports bounded.
